account: Smit et al. provide the corpus's primary null-result evidence on multi-agent debate (MAD): MAD systems in their current form do not reliably outperform self-consistency or ensembling (Smit C001; PDF PAGE 1), and Medprompt (non-debate) performs best overall across the seven evaluated datasets (Smit C003; Table 2, PDF PAGE 5). The null is qualified: on medical datasets every system except Multi-Persona beats single-agent, whereas on non-medical reasoning datasets single-agent surpasses most MAD systems (Smit C005; PDF PAGE 5). Smit also attribute the gap to hyperparameter sensitivity — agreement intensity can reverse rankings, with tuned Multi-Persona surpassing Medprompt and Self-Consistency (~15% gain on USMLE) — and they document API-variability and cost limitations (Smit C006–C008; PDF PAGES 1, 6, 9). Zhang et al. supply the boundary conditions: across 36 configurations (4 models × 9 benchmarks) no MAD method exceeds a 20% win rate over CoT, and adjusting agents/rounds does not reverse the result (Zhang C001–C002; PDF PAGES 1, 3). Task type matters: MAD performs worse on programming (only SoM/AgentVerse positive) but better on mathematical reasoning (Zhang C003; PDF PAGE 7). MAD also converts tokens less efficiently than Self-Consistency (Zhang C005; PDF PAGE 9), and model heterogeneity (Heter-MAD) consistently improves all tested MAD frameworks, with gains attributed to solving CW/WC questions (Zhang C006; PDF PAGES 11–12). These results directly conflict with Du et al.'s reported debate gains, which we reconcile through three design inferences below.

boundary_findings.narrative: Zhang et al.'s positive replication is limited: MAD outperforms SA in most conditions, but this does not translate to beating CoT or SC under matched compute. This boundary must not be absorbed as evidence that MAD generally helps; the evaluation plan must treat SA/CoT/SC as distinct baselines.

counterevidence: Smit et al. report that with hyperparameter tuning, Multi-Persona surpassed Medprompt and Self-Consistency (PDF PAGE 9), directly contradicting the global null.
Zhang et al. find that MAD frameworks outperform single-agent prompting in most conditions (34/45), aligning with prior positive results (PDF PAGE 7-8).
Zhang et al. replicate that EoT can surpass CoT on GSM8K and CommensenseQA, and AgentVerse can outperform on HumanEval (PDF PAGE 8).
